question.problem: If $f(x)$ is right-continuous at $x=3$ and $f(3)=1$, then what is $\displaystyle{\lim_{x\to 3^+}} \left(f(x)-x^2\right)?$
question.worked_solution:
Since $f(x)$ is right-continuous at $x=3,$ we must have

$$
\lim_{x\to 3^+} f(x)=f(3)=1.
$$

Consequently,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {3}^{+}}(f(x)-{x}^{2})=1-{3}^{2}=-8.\end{aligned}
$$
